page: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd is a bare metal server in the Bare Metal SSD family, featuring an AMD EPYC 9254 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with a base clock speed of 2.9 GHz and dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by a 960 GB local SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no GPUs bundled with this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong computational and memory performance. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier single-core stress-ng performance and strong multi-core results. Memory subsystem performance is highly competitive, with Passmark memory scores ranking in the top tier and large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 296.64 GB/sec. The system also excels in data processing tasks, showing top-tier single-threaded bzip3 decompression and strong multi-threaded decompression. For database workloads, it handles 72.25 million Redis SET operations per second and registers strong Passmark database operations. Large language model inference benchmarks for a small 135M model and text generation for a 7B model both rank in the top tier.

Given its bare metal architecture, dedicated resources, and high-density DDR5 memory, this server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive workloads that require direct hardware access without virtualization overhead. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive applications. Recommended workloads include large-scale database deployments, in-memory caching systems, data compression pipelines, and moderate-scale LLM inference tasks.
